newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lawmakers to consider debt reform measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lawmakers to consider debt reform measure.

text.p: California state lawmakers this week will consider legislation that would force local governments to seek voter approval for certain lease-backed debt issues.

Senate Bill 147, by Senator Ruben Ayala, a Democrat, would require local governments to obtain majority voter approval before issuing certificates of participation (COPs) backed by developer fee revenues.
The bill would also require local governments issuing COPs to inform their communities about the proposed borrowings by holding public hearings.
The bill will be considered Wednesday by the Senate Local Government Committee, which rejected the measure last month.
Since failing in March, the bill was amended to exempt debt issued by toll road agencies in Orange County and to delete other controversial provisions.
The current version of Senate Bill 147 does not impact local agencies' tax, revenue, and grant anticipation notes, traditional revenue bonds, and conduit financings.
Supporters of the measure argue that the public should have more control over COPs because this form of debt can drain local government finances.
